program: RiVive free-access supply and manufacturing portfolio

nutshell.headline: An effective rescue drug does not establish an effective marginal manufacturing gift.
nutshell.body: Central national estimate: $255,604 donor and $357,846 gross-associated resources per10 QALYs. Bay estimates are $25,560,427 and $35,784,598; SF $127,802,137 and $178,922,991. Local shares are weak priors, not identified local results.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: HRT explicitly accepts philanthropic support for free supply, lower prices and production capacity; current partners distribute its approved OTC naloxone.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: No verified current marginal price, free-dose queue, linked-person reach or causal rescue increment. Existing free supply and public naloxone may replace most nominal output.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Verify a supply-constrained, otherwise-unfunded tranche with downstream delivery and nonduplicated beneficiary exposure before treating favorable scenarios as an actionable opportunity.

summary.label: Whole gift
summary.detail: 70% free-access supply,20% price/capacity/working capital,10% partnership/other work: judgment allocations. All costs retained.

summary.label: Finite national net health
summary.detail: 245 expected unique people; one protection year; ten-year survival comparison; not245 rescues or lives saved.

summary.label: Favorable national case
summary.detail: Joint favorable assumptions, not a confidence bound or verified open opportunity.

programSection.body: Harm Reduction Therapeutics Inc (EIN82-2380699) is the nonprofit manufacturer, distinct from Remedy Alliance and Harm Reduction Therapy Center. The public financial-support contact is not a retail checkout or verified restricted free-dose offer. No inquiry or gift was submitted.

steps.title: Whole-gift portfolio
steps.detail: Allocate all charitable cash. Credit only assumed incremental free-access supply; retain other capacity and partnership costs without separate health credit.

steps.title: Supply and placement
steps.detail: Subtract replacement of existing commitments, inventory, paid orders and other funding, apply capacity caps, then high-risk placement and a pooled packs-per-unique-person allowance.

steps.title: Finite causal health
steps.detail: Compare the same people under baseline and temporarily improved effective rescue, integrating their survival difference once.

programSection.boundary: One twin pack=two single-use3mg devices;24packs/case. Packs_per_unique_person is pooled supply per unique at-risk beneficiary over the funded interval, not a clinical dose recommendation, one rescuer=one patient, or one package=one overdose. Whole gift fractions sum1. Free-access cash price includes core manufacturer logistics/admin once. Remaining capital/price-access/partnership budget retained with no quantified additional health; not another same-core overhead haircut. Funding additionality subtracts substitution of already-financed free production, existing inventory, paid orders and other funders. Manufacturing cap limits extra output. Low inventory price alone does not imply supply bottleneck. Placement is last-mile arrival in high-risk networks. Packs per unique beneficiary absorbs repeated issues/sharing and stock per beneficiary; it is an unverified linked-person planning prior. Repeated responses do not generate another survivor tail. Both scenarios begin with the same unique at-risk people alive at intervention start. Delay discounts only. Recurrent nonfatal overdose leaves the person alive; fatal opioid hazard=event rate*fatality without effective rescue*(1-effective rescue). Other mortality is separate. Improved effective rescue only during finite funded protection; afterward both arms return to identical baseline mortality. Integrate the difference in whole-person survival once to finite horizon. No lifetime rescue multiplier, reduced drug use, MOUD or brain injury benefit. Effective rescue already includes witnesses, working supply, correct use, EMS and alternative naloxone; no separate98% observed-survival or formulation-efficacy factor. Rescue increment may be negative in a diagnostic access-displacement scenario. Positive incremental-dose demand is constrained not to exceed the available device pool; assumed devices per response is a modeling budget, not medical advice. HRT manufacturing and Remedy distribution estimates are alternative marginal-gift counterfactuals, not additive claims on the same naloxone chain. Distribution capacity is held at existing baseline for HRT. A combined portfolio must assign each linked person's incremental survival once; published HRT+Remedy QALYs cannot simply be summed. Gross associated outside costs per nominal pack cover only downstream distribution/training/storage/participant inputs not already HRT-paid. Full gift plus outside allowance retained even at supply null; not exhaustive net societal cost. No double production or shipping charge, medical savings or free-stock retail valuation. Signed rescue effect and gift-date PV harms allowed. Per-person acute harm is separate from survival utility; independent harm remains at zero activity. Positive ratios are null at zero/negative Q or nonfinite ratio. Bay/SF central shares1%/.2% are weak explicit national-program beneficiary-residence priors, not observed allocation or headquarters location. Nested0<=SF<=Bay<=US. Local-zero and larger-local scenarios expose uncertainty. National survival assumptions are not validated region-specific hazards.

model.headline: Expected unique-person survival, not deaths per pack
model.body: All clinical conversion and marginal funding values are explicit judgments. FDA approval supports the pharmacologic mechanism, not manufacturer-specific effectiveness. Existing public stock and EMS enter baseline rescue; funding substitution is separately handled upstream.

equation.label: Whole-gift causal chain
equation.result: N=245 expected people; national Q=3.912297655; gross resources=$140,000.

model.inputColumnLabel: Best-estimate prior, not observed organization effect

inputs.label: gift usd
inputs.range: Reference gift; scalable only within assumed caps
inputs.basis: Ordinary unrestricted gift; entire gift retained in every numerator.

inputs.label: free access allocation
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 70% judgment: free supply is a stated philanthropic purpose, but allocation is not a verified earmark. 30–90% scenario range.

inputs.label: other capacity allocation
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 20% judgment for price access, working capital and manufacturing capacity; health unquantified, costs retained.

inputs.label: other partnership allocation
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 10% judgment for partnerships and other portfolio work; health unquantified, costs retained.

inputs.label: cash per twin pack
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: $30 planning prior, not current quote. Initial $36 is explicitly now lower; $20–45 stress range includes future full-cost uncertainty. Core production/admin/logistics included once.

inputs.label: funding additionality
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 35% prior: most nominal funding can replace sales, other donors, existing inventory or baseline free commitment; 0–70% scenarios.

inputs.label: max additional twin packs
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 5,000 additional-pack cap is a planning constraint, not verified open manufacturing capacity.

inputs.label: high risk placement
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 60% prior: downstream partners must actually place supply in high-risk networks, not simply warehouse it; 0–80% scenarios.

inputs.label: twin packs per unique person
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: Two twin packs per unique at-risk person is a pooled four-device planning allowance, not observed recipients or dosing guidance; 1–6 scenarios.

inputs.label: max unique people
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 1,000-person planning cap, not observed queue or recipient count.

inputs.label: events per person year
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 0.5 annual events is a high-risk cohort judgment; historical Medicaid recurrence 0.295/year is context, not current RiVive evidence.

inputs.label: fatality without effective rescue
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 10% counterfactual event-fatality prior, not observed fatality among treated survivors.

inputs.label: baseline effective rescue
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 80% effective rescue already available through other stock, EMS and rescuers; current public supply prevents a no-care baseline.

inputs.label: rescue increment
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: Eight percentage points is the incremental probability of effective rescue per event during protection, including event-time availability and use. Signed -5pp failure and +15pp favorable cases.

inputs.label: mean doses per incremental response
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: Two devices per incremental response is a device-budget prior, not product-specific measured consumption or clinical advice.

inputs.label: other mortality hazard
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 0.06/year is an other-cause hazard prior. Separate opioid hazard adds 0.01/year centrally; do not add opioid mortality to an all-cause rate.

inputs.label: utility
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 0.7 surviving-person utility judgment, not a disability-weight estimate for every person using opioids.

inputs.label: active years
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: One year of funded rescue protection, not ten years of active stock benefit; 0.25–1-year scenarios.

inputs.label: horizon years
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: Ten-year finite survival observation, with shared baseline mortality after protection. 1–15-year scenarios; no lifetime award.

inputs.label: delay years
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: Half-year service delay; expected cohort is already conditioned on being alive at service start. Delay discounts, not pre-service survival.

inputs.label: discount
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 3% annual health discount applied continuously via log(1.03).

inputs.label: episode harm per unique person
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 0.0002 gift-date present-value QALYs lost per unique person, acute burden separate from surviving-person utility; judgment.

inputs.label: independent harm q
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: Gift-date present-value harm not tied to activity. Central zero; explicit zero-activity -1 QALY case.

inputs.label: outside per nominal pack
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: $15 prior for downstream handling, community handoff/training and participant inputs outside manufacturer price; not HRT-paid warehouse, transport or repeat production.

inputs.label: outside other usd
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: $5,000 further associated resource allowance. Gross-associated, not exhaustive net societal cost or proven incremental expenditure.

inputs.label: bay share
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 1% weak beneficiary-residence prior, not Berkeley distributor headquarters or measured shipment allocation. Zero and3% cases.

inputs.label: sf share
inputs.range: See signed scenarios and calculator validation domain
inputs.basis: 0.2% weak beneficiary-residence prior nested in Bay share; zero and0.5% cases. Same national risk mix is not regionally validated.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Central estimates are a transparent conditional planning model, not evidence-based confidence intervals. Favorable assumptions move together; zero and harm remain possible. Inventory does not establish use, and expected unique-person counts are not observed.
model.fundingBoundary: No verified current quote or open funding tranche. Whole gift plus outside allowances remain even at null supply. Gross-associated resources include nonadditional downstream activity and are neither exhaustive nor net societal cost. Do not infer manufacture is currently the binding bottleneck.

comparisonBridge.headline: HRT and Remedy are alternatives along a shared chain
comparisonBridge.body: The existing Remedy model uses a representative four-injectable-dose-equivalent distribution bundle, not a RiVive twin pack. Its procurement, last-mile constraints and causal units cannot be copied into this manufacturer model.

equation.label: Joint-portfolio restriction
equation.expression: Combined health = survival gains for a deduplicated linked-person cohort, not Q(HRT)+Q(Remedy) for overlapping supply

inputs.label: Counterfactual
inputs.range: Zero last-mile placement to favorable delivery
inputs.basis: HRT gift changes supply conditional on baseline partner capacity; Remedy gift changes distribution conditional on its own supply baseline. Neither may receive independent full credit in a joint portfolio for the same person.

sensitivity.headline: No placement, no supply-linked health
sensitivity.detail: Resources remain. An arbitrary attribution haircut cannot replace specifying the actual bottleneck and joint counterfactual.

comparisonBridge.boundary: Do not sum either report with overlapping local naloxone cohorts. Count manufacturing price once; outside costs here exclude upstream costs already included in that price.

evidence.transfer: No manufacturer marginal deaths-per-pack or product superiority estimate.

evidence.result: Acceptability and reported experiences; no randomized mortality comparison.
evidence.transfer: No dose-use, unique-person, fatality or lower-withdrawal causal coefficient imported.

evidence.result: Repeat295/1,000person-years and fatal overdose1,154/100,000person-years; separate study all-cause778.3/10,000person-years.
evidence.transfer: Context for recurrent risk only. Model other mortality excludes overdose; cohorts are not current HRT or region-specific estimates.
Observational association not imported as individual rescue probability.

evidence.result: Existing free nasal/injectable supply; generic nasal switch April2026.
evidence.transfer: Competing effective rescue and supply replacement, not absence of care.

reservations: Current $30 cost,70% allocation,35% supply additionality,60% placement and8pp rescue increment are unverified priors.
No current free-dose queue or actual unique linked beneficiaries; central geography1% Bay/.2% SF is particularly weak.
2024 return shows $5,000 contributions and substantial sales; historic donor reliance is not evidence ordinary gifts fund all current production.
Reported PF operating expense $8,244,357 excludes $4,658,446 COGS. Combined $12,902,803 differs by $1 from reported direct charitable activity. No annual quantity permits current pack-cost inference.
HRT and Remedy health must not be added for shared people or stock.
Gross-associated resource allowance excludes unmeasured future medical and other budgets; no net societal ranking claim.
excludedBenefits: Price subsidy, manufacturing expansion and partnerships outside the credited supply tranche: costs retained, health unquantified.
No credit for historical product development, existing10% donation commitment, distributed inventory alone, or self-reported reversal counts.
No lifetime survival, reduced drug use, MOUD, infection, brain injury or speculative formulation-superiority credit.
